description: Send the same body as POST /v1/verify/text-quote (start and end are ignored) and get back exact, fuzzy or none, the score and the occurrences. Free, 30 a day per IP address. The answer is not signed and has no offsets or receipt; the paid route returns those. Free. Docs: https://vehcdj664efetfrsolne5umanq.srv.us/docs/verify-text-quote

examples.text: Refunds are paid within 14 days of purchase, to the card that was used.

case_sensitive.description: Default false; must be false with match "passages".

end.description: Optional, with start: the declared end offset, raw code points, exclusive. Give both or neither; not with match "passages".

match.description: exact; fuzzy (default), which also accepts small differences; or passages, for a paraphrased claim: the 3 passages of the text that share most of its words, scored, as evidence for you to judge (not a verdict). Not with start and end.

quote.description: Text to look for in the source, or with match "passages" the claim to find support for (max 1,000 characters after normalisation).

start.description: Optional, with end: the declared start offset of the quote in text, raw code points, 0-based. Only that slice is matched (max 1,000 code points), so the answer is whether the text at these offsets says the quote. Declared offsets are raw; result offsets are into the normalised text. If the slice misses but the quote is elsewhere in the text, result.located gives its position in the whole text. On a slice miss where a number differs, the answer carries match_verdict changed_number and nearest, the closest span on the slice with its diff. nearest offsets count into the slice's normalised text, not the whole text.

text.description: The source text you already hold, as sent (max 50,000 characters, and the whole request body is capped at 256 KB of UTF-8, so 50,000 characters of 4-byte text fit; no fetch, no normalising before hashing). Offsets count characters (code points).

paid_route.description: Path and price of the signed call.

match.description: The short answer. none means not found; its match_verdict is no_match or changed_number. The match and match_verdict pairs are: exact with exact; fuzzy with formatting_only or changed_meaning_possible; none with changed_number or no_match.

match_verdict.description: Added in T-3785. Why. The pairs with match: exact with exact; fuzzy with formatting_only (only spacing or . , ; : ! ? differ) or fuzzy with changed_meaning_possible (other words differ; review the diff); none with changed_number (a close passage differs in a number; the span and diff are in nearest) or none with no_match (no passage shares enough words). changed_number never comes with fuzzy. The field says no_match where match says none; match never says no_match, and match_verdict never says none. See the table in docs/verify-quote.md.
